reuse.why: The range handler reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment, but duplicates daily skipping and leaves the existing weekend mover alongside its replacement.

duplication.why: Daily exclusion is decided separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange, while weekend movement remains implemented in both getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getDateWithWeekendRule.

placement.why: Shared holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the server range handler also owns recurrence policy that should be shared with other occurrence consumers.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested schedule rules, range endpoint, configuration field, or their tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several occurrence paths, an unexplained three-day range expansion, and asserted schedule metadata instead of extending one typed occurrence-policy abstraction.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:getDatesInRange independently decides daily exclusions instead of sharing the policy added to shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getDateWithWeekendRule reshapes the retained getDateWithSkippedWeekend movement logic into a loop, and app.ts:getDatesInRange expresses getNextDate's daily exclusion as a flatMap filter.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily exclusion branch; getDatesInRange separately implements that exclusion, while existing upcoming-date and budget callers remain outside the complete policy.
